question: Does the prologue's imagery of three Globes of Light encode the structure of the Mafāḥiṣ?
proposition: The Mafāḥiṣ's structure is a Hermetic journey epitomized: up to the mental realm (Planet), down to the written (Pearl), then into the spoken (Peach), then a fourth part on the Letter itself.
reasoning: Melvin-Koushki says the plan is encoded in the prologue's cosmic trinity and identifies Planet, Pearl and Peach with the mental, written and spoken forms (Prologue pp.8-9).
He also says Ibn Turka declines to give a book plan (Prologue p.8), so the correspondence is his reading of imagery, not a stated plan.
His own ordering of the three Globes varies across the Prologue; only the p.9 order matches the dissertation's section order.
The dissertation's own description of the work (three sections, then a fourth) needs no such encoding (pdf p.352).
